# Results

Simulation results for energysim.

`Results` is what `energysim.world.simulate` returns.  It holds
one table per simulator (rows = recorded time points, columns = output
variables, typed float / int / bool / str), plus units and run metadata, and
offers selection, wide-frame alignment, summaries, KPIs, persistence
(Parquet / CSV / HDF5) and an interactive dashboard.

Recording during a run is done by the internal `Recorder`, which
buffers rows per simulator and converts them chunk-wise into typed NumPy
columns (optionally streaming the chunks to Parquet part files).

KPIs are pluggable:

```python {.no-test}
from energysim.results import register_kpi
register_kpi('peak_kw', lambda s, unit: float(s.max()) if unit == 'kW' else None)
```

## The Results object

Results of one co-simulation run (or an ensemble of runs).

```python
from energysim import world

sim = world(start_time=0, stop_time=3600, t_macro=900)
sim.add_signal('ramp', lambda t: [t / 3600.0], step_size=900)
res = sim.simulate()                 # a Results object; nothing is written to disk
print(res['ramp.y'])                 # pandas Series indexed by time [s]
print(res.to_frame().tail(2))        # wide frame, columns 'sim.var'
print(res.units, res.meta['seed'])   # units per variable and run metadata
```

## Access

| Expression | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `res.sims` | simulator names |
| `res.variables(sim=None)` | variable names (`'sim.var'` when *sim* is None) |
| `res['sim.var']` | `pandas.Series` indexed by time |
| `res['sim']` | `pandas.DataFrame` (index `time`) |
| `res.to_frame(...)` | wide frame on the union time grid, columns `'sim.var'` |
| `res.units` / `res.meta` | units per `'sim.var'` and run metadata |
| `res.summary()` / `res.kpis()` |  |

Time is in seconds (float) unless ``start_datetime`` is set, in which case
a ``DatetimeIndex`` is returned.

## Methods

| Method | Summary |
|---|---|
| `concat(results, keys=None, params=None)` | Combine several runs into an ensemble with a `run` dimension. |
| `dashboard(path=None, open=False, max_points=5000, offline=False, title='energysim Result Explorer')` | Write the interactive HTML dashboard and return its path. |
| `is_ensemble` (property) | - |
| `items()` |  |
| `keys()` |  |
| `kpis(names=None, sims=None, variables=None)` | Evaluate registered KPIs for every numeric variable. |
| `load(path)` | Load results written by `save` / a run directory / an HDF5 file. |
| `meta` (property) | - |
| `params` (property) | Run parameters (one row per run, index = run key). |
| `run(key)` | One run of an ensemble, by key (or by position if *key* is not a key). |
| `run_dir` (property) | - |
| `run_keys` (property) | - |
| `runs` (property) | Per-run `Results` (a single run returns `[self]`). |
| `save(path, format='auto')` | Save to *path* and return its absolute path. |
| `sims` (property) | - |
| `start_datetime` (property) | - |
| `status` (property) | - |
| `summary()` | Per-variable `count, min, max, mean, last` (and unit / dtype). |
| `to_csv(directory)` | Write one CSV file per simulator (+ `meta.json`) into *directory*. |
| `to_frame(sims=None, variables=None, resample=None, ffill=True, start_datetime=None)` | Wide `DataFrame` with columns `'sim.var'` on the union of all time points. |
| `to_hdf(path)` | Write all simulator tables into one HDF5 file (requires `tables`). |
| `to_parquet(directory)` | Write one Parquet file per simulator (+ `meta.json`) into *directory*. |
| `units` (property) | - |
| `values()` |  |
| `variables(sim=None)` | Variable names of *sim*, or all `'sim.var'` names when *sim* is None. |

## Built-in KPIs

Registered KPIs (add your own with `energysim.register_kpi`): `min`, `max`, `mean`, `time_weighted_mean`, `energy_kwh`, `energy_kwh_trapz`.

## Persistence formats

| Format | Method | Extra needed |
|---|---|---|
| Parquet + `meta.json` | `res.save(path)` / `res.to_parquet(path)` | `pip install energysim[results]` (`save` falls back to CSV without pyarrow) |
| CSV | `res.to_csv(path)` | - |
| HDF5 | `res.to_hdf(path)` | `pip install energysim[hdf5]` |
| Reload | `Results.load(path)` | - |

## Ensembles

A `Results` object can hold several runs (`is_ensemble`, `res.run(i)`, `Results.concat`). `Ensemble` and `Sweep` build such objects from many runs; see [Ensembles and sweeps](ensemble.md).
